items: **Instance variables** belong to the object; **local variables** live and die inside a method.
**`this`** names the current object and resolves parameter/field shadowing, `this.name = name;`
**`private`** members are usable only inside the class; **`public`** members are usable anywhere.
**Encapsulation** = private data + public methods. It exists to make invalid states unreachable, not to add ceremony.
Provide accessors and mutators **deliberately**: omitting a setter is often the right design.
Class-type variables hold **references**, so compare objects with **`equals()`**, not `==`.
